title: The two-sided ideal generated by the commutators of the Askey-Wilson algebra coincides with the kernel of its polynomial quotient

core_obligations: Set up the comparison: let Gamma be the kernel of the homomorphism to the polynomial algebra, a two-sided ideal, and observe that every commutator lies in Gamma because the target is commutative, whence the two-sided ideal generated by the commutators is contained in Gamma (proof lines 2811-2834).

Build a complement: the images of the monomials A^i B^j C^k form a basis of the polynomial algebra, so those monomials form a basis of a complement M with Delta = M + Gamma direct (proof lines 2835-2850).

Show the sum fills the algebra: since A, B, C generate the algebra, it suffices to rewrite every word x_1...x_n modulo the two-sided ideal generated by the commutators, which the proof does by successively swapping adjacent letters and identifying the resulting class with A^i B^j C^k in M (proof lines 2851-2883).

Conclude the coincidence: combining the inclusion of the ideal in Gamma with the directness of Delta = M + Gamma forces the two-sided ideal generated by the commutators to equal Gamma (proof lines 2884-2890).
proof_roadmap: Include the commutator ideal in the kernel and produce a monomial complement of the kernel (proof lines 2811-2850).
Show that any word lies in the complement plus the commutator ideal, and conclude by directness (proof lines 2851-2890).
difficulty_reason: The proposition compares two objects attached to the universal Askey-Wilson algebra: the two-sided ideal generated by its commutators, and the kernel of the homomorphism onto the three-variable polynomial algebra (statement lines 2792-2808). The proof first observes that the commutator ideal sits inside that kernel because the target is commutative, then constructs a complement from the monomials A^i B^j C^k, which form a basis on the polynomial side, and finally shows that every word in the generators can be rewritten modulo the commutator ideal into that complement by successively swapping adjacent letters (proof lines 2811-2883). The step that carries the content is the rewriting, since it is what upgrades an inclusion into an equality, and it is done by hand on words rather than by citing a general theorem. The directness of the sum then finishes the proof. H2.
